kicker: Decision models from a serving flag

scenes.headline: How any model becomes a decision model
scenes.sub: SGLang's /v1/score: one prefill, read at the tokens you name.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Jiggle! People are turning ordinary language models into decision models with a single serving call. Here's what that call actually computes.

scenes.text: The readout is a serving feature, not a model feature: one prefill, then read the next-token probabilities at the candidate tokens you name.
scenes.mark: a serving feature, not a model feature
scenes.say: The idea: the readout is a serving feature, not a model feature. One prefill, then read the probabilities of the tokens you name.

steps.say: You send a prompt and your options' token ids. The server runs one prefill with max new tokens at zero.
At the last position, the model has a logit for every vocabulary entry.
It reads only the rows you named: each one's real probability, so they needn't sum to one.

steps.note: the mass on every other token is the model declining
steps.say: Turn on softmax and the slice is renormalised. That deletes the mass on every other token, which was the model declining.

left.title: Options in the prompt
items: Lettered options; read the letter tokens
One pass, all options share a context
left.say: Put lettered options in the prompt and read the letters: one pass, but order matters. Reversing it changed ten of thirty-six answers.

right.title: One prompt per option
items: Read Yes or No after each option
A pass each; no option sees another
The scorer's isolation, with nothing trained
right.say: Put each option in its own prompt and read Yes: a pass per option, and none can see another. Isolation, with nothing trained.

scenes.title: Where the 63x comes from
scenes.say: Where the headline speedup comes from.

parts.note: baseline: 15.21 ms for each of G generated tokens
parts.say: The baseline types its answer one token at a time, about fifteen milliseconds each.

parts.note: scored path: one prefill, then every branch in one batched pass
parts.say: The scored path is one prefill, then every candidate branch in one batched pass.

parts.note: you pick the ratio by picking the workload
parts.say: So the ratio is just how many tokens the baseline typed: two hundred twenty-six gave about sixty-three times.

scenes.text: The serving half is free on SGLang; calibration needs labelled outcomes, so a published calibration number shows who did the rest.

recap: One prefill; read the probabilities of named tokens
Where the options go picks the model family
Calibration can't come from the serving layer
scenes.say: To recap: one pass, read at the tokens you name, and calibration still costs labels.
